_meta: Two short documents packed into one training sequence, used to show why packing needs a block-diagonal (document-aware) attention mask on top of the causal mask, or tokens in one document attend back into an unrelated document packed before them -- cross-document contamination. Training a transformer on short sequences wastes compute: pad each to the block length and most of the tensor is padding the model still runs attention over. The standard fix is PACKING -- concatenate several short documents into one full-length sequence so almost every position holds a real token. But packing changes what 'the sequence' means. With only the usual causal mask (each position may attend to itself and everything before it), a token at the start of the second document can attend to every token of the first document, because they now sit in the same sequence -- even though the two documents are unrelated. The model then learns to predict document B's tokens using document A's content, which is leakage: it never happens at inference (where B arrives on its own) and it teaches spurious cross-document dependencies. The fix is a block-diagonal attention mask: in addition to the causal constraint, a position may attend to another only if they belong to the SAME document (segment). Attention becomes block-diagonal -- each document attends only within itself -- so packing gains its efficiency without contaminating across boundaries. tokens are the packed token ids; segment is each token's document id (which packed document it belongs to). A causal mask allows attention from i to j when j <= i; a block-diagonal mask additionally requires segment[i] == segment[j]. tokens and segment are the fixture; both attention masks, the cross-document and intra-document edge counts, and each position's allowed attention are computed.
